Reporting scope distinguishes requested selection, known/discovered work, incomplete collection and prepared-source execution.

Test coverage — pass. Independently reconciled 1343 baseline rows:1337 native cases plus6 non-case checks, all started/passed, unique identities equal the expected worker set. All1313 M1 native cases appear exactly once, including all95 adapters;24 reporting additions explain the baseline increase. Existing catalog coverage allocation accounts for scoped/full adapters and direct/full Node callers without changing ordinary selected membership. Two later reporting additions passed as isolated reviewer workers with costs5888ms and257ms, bringing current accounted native population to1339. No retained product case or direct entrypoint disappeared.

Edge cases — pass. Focused reporting proof covers unknown mode/status and invalid duration values, alias agreement/conflict, stable ranking/ties and unsuccessful rows, unstarted dependencies, missing-command attempt cost, timeout and handled interruption, partial collection without invented identities, selection errors, concurrent reservation, invalid destination types and selected-input collisions. Final-capture clock injection proves the measurement extends beyond the earlier poll timestamp. Actual short-lived workers and native case receipts complement deterministic arithmetic.

Error handling — pass. Controlled failures retain nonzero selection/execution precedence, known results and incomplete scope. Report serialization/replacement failure preserves prior bytes and turns success into exit1 without erasing an existing worker exit7. Prepared coordinator/child handoff retains nonzero outer or child status and actual prepared subject, and missing private report cannot imply success. Worker failures, timeout and unstarted dependencies remain explicit rather than receiving fabricated free successful durations.

Architecture and maintainability — pass. The shell now delegates selection/preparation and reporting lifetime to the existing executor, enabling reservation before work and one final writer. Private native discovery and shared-budget scheduling remain the execution path; the new reporting tests are imported by the existing aggregate and have an explicit selector classification. No persistent benchmark cache, scenario-driven execution engine or permanent method ledger is introduced.

Backward compatibility — pass within assessed mode/caller scope. Existing selector172 and full pre-correction executor76 cases passed in the complete baseline; existing legacy report readers and package/native suites passed. Canonical per-row IDs, command/status/exit/phase, child_durations, cache label and null historical baseline/delta fields remain. Both generic and legacy destinations are removed from children while unrelated environment and bounded nested workers remain. Prepared producer/consumer tests retain requested versus prepared source and native direct Python/Node behavior; no live release or provider action is claimed.

Security and preservation — pass after required correction. Report admission rejects unsafe traversal, symlink/nonregular/multiple-link targets, absent parents, source/input/capture ownership conflicts and active destination reservations. Publication serializes first, uses an owned sibling temporary and pinned parent descriptor, then atomic replacement; cleanup identifies the owned lock. First-pass late collision previously allowed an overwrite; the exact corrected guard now irrevocably prevents publication after such collision. Independent public reproduction and native regression measurements prove preserved bytes and cleanup. The finding is reporter-resolved without altering its original evidence.

The baseline exercised actual private adapter archive build/validation and existing packed npm/installed CLI suites. The four-line report guard and two additional reporting tests do not change generated consumer content; post-correction targeted safety proof is appropriate, and no retroactive generated-output claim is made.

All original M1 evidence entries are semantically identical in the additive evidence container; the old code-review-m1 subject identity is preserved and relied on only for unchanged M1 claims.
